techStack: React 19.0.0, TypeScript 5.7.2, Vite 6.2, Vitest 3.2.4 with jsdom
State management: useState + useContext + useCallback — no external state library
favouriteIds and pendingIds are both Set<string> held in useState; always create a new Set to trigger re-render
Functional updater pattern already established: setFavouriteIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); ...; return next; })
Strict TS flags: noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters — introduced symbols must actually be used
verbatimModuleSyntax: true — type-only imports need the 'type' keyword
Tests stub global fetch via vi.stubGlobal; implementation must use window.fetch (not an injected dep)
Build command: tsc -b && vite build; test command: vitest run
features: toggleFavourite (current): reads favouriteIds → computes wasAdded → optimistic setFavouriteIds update → try/catch fetch → on success: setError(null) → on failure: setError(msg) only — no revert
setPendingIds is defined (line 27) but never called anywhere in the file; pendingIds is always an empty Set
isPending(productId) reads pendingIds.has(productId) — always returns false because pendingIds is never populated
FavouriteButton already fully wired: disabled={pending}, aria-label swap, Loading span — just needs isPending to return true during in-flight requests
What must not regress: localStorage hydration (useLayoutEffect), localStorage sync (useEffect), isFavourite, FavouritesPage results-count, all 4 happy-path tests in favouriteRevert.test.tsx
Bug 1: no setPendingIds calls — isPending always false, FavouriteButton never disabled
Bug 2: catch block does not call setFavouriteIds — optimistic update never reverted on fetch rejection
architecture: FavouritesContext.tsx: Provider + useFavouritesContext hook; toggleFavourite is useCallback with [favouriteIds] dep array
toggleFavourite uses async/await with try/catch — no finally block currently exists; one must be added
Functional updater already used for setFavouriteIds optimistic update (lines 51–59) — same pattern required in catch revert
Fix location: all changes are within toggleFavourite in FavouritesContext.tsx (lines ~46–83)
Order of operations in fixed version: setPendingIds(add) → optimistic setFavouriteIds → try fetch → catch: setFavouriteIds(revert) + setError → finally: setPendingIds(remove)
Only src/benchmark-frontend/src/context/FavouritesContext.tsx may be modified; FavouriteButton.tsx, FavouritesPage.tsx, and tests/ are read-only
edgeCases: Concurrent toggles on different products: catch revert must use functional updater (prev => ...) not a snapshot Set captured before the toggle — prevents overwriting a concurrent successful toggle on another product
Add-failure revert: catch must call setFavouriteIds(prev => { const next = new Set(prev); next.delete(productId); return next; }) when wasAdded is true
Remove-failure revert: catch must call setFavouriteIds(prev => new Set(prev).add(productId)) when wasAdded is false
finally ordering: catch reverts favouriteIds first, then finally removes from pendingIds — both execute on failure path; correct because finally always runs after catch

Double-toggle guard: button is disabled while isPending(productId) is true — a second call cannot reach toggleFavourite for the same productId; if it somehow did, adding an already-present id to a Set is a no-op and the finally cleanup correctly removes it once
Non-2xx responses where fetch does not reject: out of scope per requirements — do not add response.ok checks

Happy-path tests (favouriteRevert.test.tsx × 4) use a global fetch stub that always resolves — the fix must not break these; setPendingIds adds/removes around each fetch call so pendingIds is always empty after test completes
